title: Rear Seat Cushion Cover: Removal and Refitting
introduction:
The rear cushion cover has several hidden anchors: J-clips and pin-type retainers underneath, plus hook-and-loop strips against the foam. I think of it as a fitted sheet with a more serious attachment system—pulling harder at the top will not release what is still fastened underneath.

Start by removing the cushion from the car, then work through the attachments in order. The underside illustration maps the clips and retainers; the peeled-back cover illustration shows the hook-and-loop locations. The key is to free the cover while leaving those strips attached to the foam.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Before service, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from accidentally starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges, including any such edges encountered on the cushion frame. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: Remove the rear seat cushion before releasing its cover. Refer to: [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Move both front seats fully forward for access. At the front edge of the rear cushion, locate the locking tabs on both sides and press them in to release the cushion from the floor. The tabs must be pressed in before lifting; lifting against locked tabs may damage them. Once released, lift and release the cushion, then remove it from the car. This exposes the underside attachments needed for the cover work.

edits.text: Release the cover's J-clips and pin-type retainers from the underside of the seat cushion frame. Then pass the J-clip attaching straps through the openings in the cushion foam.
edits.why: Use the underside illustration to locate the attachments around the frame edges and at the strap ends; the round pin-type retainers are also shown in close-up. Passing the released straps through the foam openings frees their route through the cushion before the cover is lifted away.

edits.text: NOTICE: Separate the cushion cover from the hook-and-loop strips carefully. Careless separation can tear the strips away from the seat cushion foam pad.
edits.why: The intended separation is between the mating hook-and-loop surfaces. The strips attached to the foam must stay there.

edits.text: Carefully separate the seat cushion cover from the hook-and-loop strips, leaving the strips attached to the foam pad. Once those attachments are free, remove the cushion cover.
edits.why: The peeled-back illustration shows the strips following the cushion's recessed contours. I use that pattern to follow the remaining attachment points as the cover comes away, rather than treating a resistant area as an invitation to yank.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence. Position the cover on the cushion foam and reconnect the hook-and-loop strips. Pass the J-clip attaching straps back through the foam openings, then reattach the J-clips and pin-type retainers to the underside of the frame. Reinstall the rear seat cushion by reversing its removal, lowering it into position and reengaging the front locking tabs. During installation, make sure the seatbelt webbing is not twisted and the seatbelts and buckles remain accessible to the occupant.
edits.why: The cover attachments restore its position on the foam; the floor locking tabs secure the complete cushion in the car. Before finishing, check that the cover attachments and cushion tabs are engaged, and that no belt or buckle has been trapped beneath the cushion. The belt routing requirement comes from the linked rear cushion procedure.
